title: Mitigating Simplicity Bias in Deep Learning for Improved OOD Generalization and Robustness

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing model reliance on simple spurious features (e.g., image background, texture, or color) versus complex invariant features (e.g., object shape) by measuring out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization and accuracy gaps on datasets like Waterbirds, ImageNet-9, and Colored-MNIST.

Evaluating worst-group and OOD accuracy on datasets where gender acts as a spurious feature (CelebA, Adult-Confounded, CivilComments), and measuring Social Norm Bias (SNoB) by calculating the Spearman rank correlation between gender pronouns and occupation predictions on the Bios dataset.
Evaluating worst-group and out-of-distribution accuracy across different racial subgroups (e.g., Black vs. non-Black individuals) using the Adult-Confounded and CivilComments datasets.
Measuring worst-group accuracy for toxicity classification on the CivilComments dataset specifically for comments mentioning Christian, Muslim, and other religious identities.
Measuring worst-group accuracy for toxicity classification on the CivilComments dataset for comments containing mentions of LGBTQ identities.
